title: Improve dedicated autoscaler SLO handling, burst controls, and utilization reporting
author: Evan Chen
release_notes: Adjusts autoscaler SLO evaluation window and exposes per-fleet burst utilization metrics; no API breaking changes.
description:
Background: Dedicated fleets have seen intermittent SLA misses during short bursts when token-bucket smoothing and SLO evaluation windows are misaligned with real traffic patterns. This PR tightens SLO evaluation, improves burst controls, and adds utilization reporting to aid capacity planning.

What this change does: - Change SLO evaluation to a rolling 5m window with 30s step (previously 1m fixed windows) to reduce noisy alerts and better reflect transient burst behavior. - Add per-fleet `dedicated_burst_utilization` metric (gauge) and tags for fleet_id/region/priority to the observability layer. - Implement token-bucket smoothing for priority queues to prevent aggressive instantaneous bursts from triggering autoscale overshoot. - Expose a new autoscaler debug endpoint /internal/autoscaler/metrics that returns summarized token-bucket state and recent scaling events (read-only, auth gated). - Refactor autoscaler evaluation loop for clearer boundaries between throughput guarantees and burst headroom calculation.

Motivation: Customers require predictable throughput guarantees while preserving the ability to absorb short bursts without unnecessary scale-ups. Better metrics and smoothing reduce cost by preventing oscillation and give operators actionable signals.

Checklist: - [x] Update SLO evaluation logic and unit tests (ENG-4211) - [x] Add burst utilization metric and dashboards wiring - [x] Implement token-bucket smoothing algorithm with feature flag - [x] Add integration test that simulates burst traffic and verifies no excess scale-ups - [x] Add docs snippet to dedicated autoscaler README - [x] Sanity-check security for new debug endpoint

Notes: This is behind a feature flag `autoscaler.smoothing.enabled` defaulting to false in prod for a staged rollout. The new metric is additive and does not change existing telemetry nameset.
commits: Adjust SLO window evaluation to use 5m sliding window (ENG-4211)
Introduce token-bucket smoothing for priority queues (feature-flagged)
Refactor autoscaler loop and add integration test for throughput guarantees
review_comments: Sara Martinez: Can you explain why we chose 5m instead of 3m? Concerned about detection latency for sustained regressions.

Author (Evan Chen): 5m was chosen after benchmarking traffic traces from 3 customers; 3m reduced noise but still caused oscillation under bursty tails. We can make the window configurable per-fleet; added a follow-up note in ENG-4320.
Liam O'Connor: Please add a unit test covering the smoothing edge case where burst tokens are partially refunded after a drop in traffic.
Author: Added test case in controller_test.go and integration test that simulates token refund scenarios.
Priya Patel: Approving after verifying metrics and dashboard wiring in staging. Observability team ran queries against the new metric and labels look good.
CI Bot: unit tests failed (TestAutoscalerEdgeCases) on first run; rerun succeeded after test timeout bump.
summary: Feature-flagged smoothing, SLO window change, new metrics and dashboards to reduce unnecessary scaling and improve capacity visibility.
notes_for_ops: Enable autoscaler.smoothing.enabled=false by default. Ramp to true for low-traffic fleets first, validate dedicated_burst_utilization telemetry and dashboard before global rollout.
risk_assessment: Low/Medium: Behavioral change in scaling heuristics behind feature flag; new observability only. Rolling back the flag reverts behavior.
